consensus_summary: No single settled symbolic meaning; most common/primary senses across responses are (1) day as realm/time of light, righteousness, moral clarity and wakeful action contrasted with night/darkness, and (2) the eschatological Day of the Lord as divine judgment/salvation, plus frequent alternatives of extended periods, day-year equivalence in prophecy, and day=1000 years.
book_summary: Day is the time of light, exposure, and accountable action (opposite Night); in prophetic counts it may also scale to a year or a thousand years by context.
consensus_core_identification: Time/realm of light and righteous/accountable action (vs night), with secondary time-period and prophetic scalings
book_core_identification: Time of light, exposure, and accountable action (vs night), with prophetic scaling to year or thousand years
rationale: Minimum cores identify the same primary referent (light/righteous/accountable sphere opposed to night) that multiple consensus responses already list as primary or dominant alternative; the book's prophetic scalings are likewise already enumerated as common/minority alternatives in every consensus response. Differences are only wording and the book's omission of a separate Day-of-the-Lord heading, which does not replace or contradict the shared core.
strongest_objection: Some consensus responses elevate 'Day of the Lord' or pure temporal relativization as equally or more primary, so the book's tighter phrasing could be read as selective emphasis rather than full equivalence.
